paper.title: Causal Bandits: Learning Good Interventions via Causal Inference

settings.name_in_paper: Parallel bandit (causal bandit with parallel graph)
unmapped: N independent binary causes X_i ~ Bernoulli(q_i) of reward Y; q unknown to learner
actions: do() plus all size-1 interventions do(X_i=j), i.e. 2N+1 arms
after each intervention, learner observes all non-intervened variables X (post-action causal side observations) in addition to Y
learner knows the causal graph and N
settings.definition_quote: The causal model for this class of problems has $N$ binary variables $\{ X_1, \ldots, X_N \}$ where each $X_i \in \{0,1\}$ are independent causes of a reward variable $Y \in \set{0,1}$ ... the set of allowable actions are all size 0 and size 1 interventions ... The objective of the learner is to minimise the simple regret $R_T = \mu^* - \E{\mu_{\hat a^*_T}}.$

actions: do() plus all size-1 interventions, 2N+1 arms
learner observes all non-intervened variables after each intervention

settings.name_in_paper: General causal bandit (known graph, known conditional interventional distributions of parents of Y)
unmapped: arbitrary known causal DAG over finite-valued variables; actions are interventions do(X=x) from allowed set A
learner observes all non-intervened variables after each intervention
learner knows the conditional interventional distributions P(Pa_Y | a) for all actions a (but not P(Y|a))
settings.definition_quote: We now consider the more general problem where the graph structure is known, but arbitrary. ... we assume the conditional interventional distributions $\P{\parents{Y}|a}$ (but not $\P{Y|a}$) are known.

algorithms.name: General Algorithm (Algorithm 2, truncated importance weighted estimator)

symbols.m_q: m(q) = min{tau : |I_tau| <= tau}, I_tau = {i : min(q_i,1-q_i) < 1/tau}; number of 'difficult' actions
symbols.N_var: number of binary cause variables N (2N+1 actions)

results.notes: Proof gives explicit 6m/T + sqrt(32 m/T log(NT/m)). Depends on q via m(q), which is unknown and estimated by the algorithm; worst case over reward functions. Simple regret mu* - E[mu_{hat a}].

conditions: holds for every T and every q; worst case over reward functions r

source.label: thm:lower
source.quote: For all $T$, $\vec{q}$ and all strategies, there exists a reward function such that \simpleregret \in \Omega\left(\sqrt{\frac{m(\vec{q})}{T}}\right)\,.

results.notes: Worst case over reward function for fixed q; depends on q through m(q).

symbols.m_eta: m(eta) = max_a E_a[P{Pa_Y(X)|a}/Q{Pa_Y(X)}], Q mixture of interventional distributions under sampling distribution eta

conditions: P(Pa_Y | a) known for all actions

source.label: thm:general
source.quote: If Algorithm \ref{alg:general} is run with $B \in \R^{\calA}$ given by $B_a = \sqrt{\frac{m(\eta)T}{\log\left(2T|\calA|\right)}}\,.$ \simpleregret \in \bigo{\sqrt{\frac{m(\eta)}{T} \log\left(2T|\calA|\right)}}\,.

results.notes: K = |A| number of allowed interventions. Proof gives (sqrt2+4)sqrt(m(eta)/T log(2T|A|)) + 1/T. Proposition 4: m(eta*) <= |A|; Proposition 9: in parallel bandit m(eta*) <= 2m(q).
